To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synthesis of phospholipid by the cells was constant, whereas the synthesis of the phosphorylated derivative decreased during growth.

the rate of choline phosphorylation by choline kinase of Novikoff rat hepato-ma cells decreases during the growth cycle of a culture, and that the rate of phosphatidycholine synthesis is constant during this cycle.

the synthesis of phosphoryl-choline by Novikoff hepatoma cells decreases during growth in culture, and that newly synthesized phosphatid-ylcholine is incorporated into the membranes of cellular mitochondria, plasma membrane fragments and membranous structures of intermediate density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the synthesis of choline-containing phospholipids by Novikoff hepatoma cells during growth in suspension and with their distribution among cellular membranes.
the metabolism of choline and phosphatidylinositol during the growth cycle of Novikoff rat ascites hepatoma cells in suspension culture, and their role in the formation of cellular membranes.
the synthesis and incorporation of choline into phospholipids during cell growth in suspension culture and its relation to the growth of the mitochondria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the cells studied the rate of synthesis and turnover of phosphatidycholine was relatively constant throughout the growth cycle, while that of phosphorylcholin decreased markedly.
the synthesis of phospholipid and protein components of the cell membrane is not a random event, but a highly regulated process.

choline kinase activity and choline incorporation into phosphorylcholines decrease progressively during the growth cycle of rat hepatoma cells in suspension culture, while phosphatidyl-choline synthesis and the incorporation of the latter into membranes remain constant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the rate of choline incorporation into phosphorylcholines and phosphatidycholines of the membranes of Novikoff hepatoma cells is dependent on the rate of cell growth, that the synthesis of phosphoryl-choline and phosphatidy-choline is controlled by different regulatory mechanisms, and that newly synthesized phosphatidycholine is incorporated rapidly into cellular membranes.

during growth of the hepatoma cells in suspension culture, the rate of phospholipid synthesis decreases as the culture becomes denser, but that this is not due to a decreased rate of choline incorporation into phospholipids.

the choline kinase activity is an important determinant of the rate of growth of the cells in suspension culture, that newly synthesized phosphatidycholine is rapidly and uniformly distributed among cellular membrane structures, and that the mitochondria grow in number and increase in density as they mature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of synthesis and incorporation of phosphatidycholine into the various cellular membranes is not a limiting factor in the growth and division of the Novikoff rat ascites hepatoma cells.
the rate of choline metabolism and phospholipid synthesis in the cells is closely related to the cell growth cycle.
the synthesis of phospholipid in the form of phosphorylcholines and phosphatidycholines is an integral part of the growth process.
